core.title: Name produced/consumed plan artifacts by their nature: activity-verb for events, data-noun for state, plural for collections
core.given: A plan artifact of one unit of the product declares a produce block (artifacts the unit creates and owns) or a consume block (artifacts it consumes).
core.when: The planner adds, renames, reviews or validates an artifact name there, or changes an artifact's nature (event vs state) or cardinality.
core.then: Name each such artifact by its nature, using the interface's namespace-qualified artifact name shape: a past-tense activity-verb name for a signal/event, a noun/adjective data-noun name for state/data, and a plural name for a collection.
prefer: Produce entries follow the interface's produce entry shape: the artifact's name plus the visibility of what is produced.
Consume entries follow the interface's consume entry shape: the artifact's name plus the source it is consumed from (another unit, an external system, or internal).
Reuse the producer's exact name on every consume side.

Adjective-like participles describing current state are valid state names (e.g. namespace:chosen, namespace:remaining); a dotted sub-path after the namespace segment is allowed (e.g. namespace:state.current).
avoid: Present/imperative verbs for events; action-describing names for state/data; noun forms for signals.
Singular names for collections; names lacking the namespace prefix required by the artifact name shape.
core.why: Consistent naming makes an artifact's nature (event vs state vs collection) legible from its name alone, so consumers know whether they respond to a signal or read data.
evidence: Every produce entry follows the produce entry shape (name plus visibility) and every consume entry follows the consume entry shape (name plus source).

Each signal/event name uses a past-tense activity verb after the namespace segment; each state/data name uses a data noun/adjective (adjective-like participles describing state allowed); each collection is plural.
A reviewer can tell from the name alone whether consumers respond to a signal or read data, including for pre-existing artifacts and artifacts whose nature or cardinality changed.
verification: Semantic check, no mechanical detector in the reference realization: deciding whether a name segment is a past-tense activity verb, a noun or adjective (including adjective-like participles describing state), or a plural, and whether the artifact is a signal or data, requires LLM/reviewer judgement.

Meaning-based classification for participle forms: an adjective-like participle describing current state/data counts as a data-noun (state) name; a past-tense verb reporting that something happened counts as an event name.

Scope: the rule applies when produce/consume declarations are authored or modified and when existing declarations are reviewed or validated; a pre-existing mismatch found during review triggers the rule just like a new one.

Observation needs: name additions/renames require a diff-level observer on the interface entry name fields; a change of an artifact's nature or cardinality under an unchanged name requires observing the artifact's description/contract plus semantic judgement.

values: plan artifact declaring a produce/consume interface
existing produce/consume artifact changes nature (event <-> state) or cardinality (single <-> collection) without being renamed
artifact name (new or pre-existing) whose form does not match its nature (event vs state vs collection)

fires: Planner adds a new entry to a unit's produce block
Planner adds a new entry to a unit's consume block
Planner renames an existing produced or consumed artifact
Planner changes an existing artifact from state to an event (or vice versa) while keeping its name
Planner changes an existing artifact from a single item to a collection (or vice versa) while keeping its name
Planner authors a unit plan that declares which signals and data the unit emits or reads
Planner reviews or validates the existing produce/consume declarations of a unit
A review finds a pre-existing produce/consume name whose form does not match the artifact's nature or cardinality
doesNotFire: Editing the unit's plan artifact for unrelated reasons (e.g. wording-only description edits or edits confined to the unit's other plan documents) when produce/consume names and artifact nature/cardinality are untouched AND the task is not a review/validation of the interface and no naming mismatch has been found
Naming code-level identifiers (functions, classes, variables) that are not produce/consume artifacts

profileRequirements.meaning: Name shape of an artifact declared in a produce/consume interface: a namespace segment (the owning domain), then the artifact name; a dotted sub-path may follow.
profileRequirements.bunValue: 'domain:artifact-name'; a dotted sub-path after the domain is allowed (e.g. domain:state.current)

profileRequirements.meaning: Produce/consume constructs of the stack's plan syntax: entry shapes of the interface blocks, i.e. name plus visibility on the produce side, name plus source on the consume side (including the source vocabulary).
profileRequirements.bunValue: produce: array of {name: 'domain:artifact-name', to: 'internal|external'}; consume: array of {name: 'domain:artifact-name', from: 'capability:slug|system:external|internal'}

neutralityNotes: The naming-by-nature obligation is semantic and fully neutral; only three things are concrete. (1) The interface artifact name shape and the produce/consume entry shapes are plan-format data carried by two profile keys: urn.artifact for the namespace-qualified name shape, and the map entry idiom.plan_syntax#interface_entry for the produce/consume entry schemas, since the vocabulary's idiom.plan_syntax map explicitly covers produce/consume constructs of plan artifacts (revised round 3: the entry schemas were previously mis-keyed as urn.grammar#interface_entry, which is for URN/identifier grammar only). (2) 'product capability' is neutralized to 'unit' / 'plan artifact'; the concrete interface-declaring kinds instantiate from roles.plan_artifact.kinds. (3) Verbatim application examples (match:started, decision:chosen, ...) and the planner-prompt quotes stay only in the Bun reference (bunOnly). doesNotFire's 'DESIRED OUTCOME edits' was generalized to 'edits confined to the unit's other plan documents' (the concrete kind is profile data). The produce/consume block structure remains operative here per bun.json's splitSuggestion (planner.interface.produce-consume-shape); the neutral core preserves it via given, prefer[0]/[1] and evidence[0] plus the entry-shape profile key, so no obligation is dropped or added. Round 2: the verb 'react' in why and evidence[2] was rephrased to 'respond' because it collides with a framework name and read as a stack leak; the meaning is unchanged.
